RT by @Mdais: On October 8, 2023 - one day after the Hamas massacre - pediatricians at Israel's National Human Milk Bank realized something no milk bank in the world had ever faced: dozens of healthy babies whose mothers had been murdered, abducted to Gaza, wounded, or called up for emergency IDF duty. The bank, operated by Magen David Adom, Israel's National Emergency Service, tripled its activity overnight - recruiting over 200 new donors, running MDA motorcycles through missile fire to collect milk daily, and working around the clock to ensure every baby received safe, screened donor breast milk. One of the babies' mothers was an Israeli Air Force Apache helicopter pilot who cut short her maternity leave to fly combat missions. "Giving of your own milk, giving part of yourself while nursing your own baby is the height of unconditional love," said the bank's chairman. More than 80% of families said the donated milk helped them cope with the consequences of the war. "They said they felt the whole country supported them." This is Israel. 🇮🇱🤍 @Mdais

استضافت كلية الدفاع الوطني العميد فريدريك تشو، نائب السكرتير للسياسات في وزارة الدفاع بجمهورية سنغافورة، لإلقاء محاضرة بعنوان "آفاق الدفاع في سنغافورة ونموذج الدفاع الشامل". وتناول العميد فريدريك تشو خلال المحاضرة أبرز ملامح السياسة الدفاعية السنغافورية، ومفهوم الدفاع الشامل ودوره في تعزيز جاهزية الدولة وقدرتها على مواجهة مختلف التحديات والتهديدات، إلى جانب استعراض عدد من التجارب والرؤى المرتبطة بالتخطيط الاستراتيجي والأمن والدفاع. وشهدت المحاضرة تفاعلاً وحواراً مع منتسبي الكلية، بما أسهم في تبادل الخبرات والمعارف حول التجربة الدفاعية السنغافورية. وتأتي هذه المحاضرة في إطار حرص كلية الدفاع الوطني على تعزيز التعاون وتبادل الخبرات الدولية وإثراء برامجها الأكاديمية والاستراتيجية. The National Defence College hosted Brigadier Frederick Choo, Deputy Secretary for Policies at the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Singapore, who delivered a lecture entitled “Singapore’s Defence Outlook and the Total Defence Model.” During the lecture, Brigadier Frederick Choo highlighted key aspects of Singapore’s defence policies, and discussed the concept of Total Defence and its role in strengthening the nation’s preparedness and ability to respond to a range of challenges and threats. He also shared a number of experiences and insights relating to strategic planning, security and defence. The lecture featured an engaging discussion and interaction with the College’s personnel, contributing to an exchange of knowledge and expertise on Singapore’s defence experience.
